title: Rust: Strategy Pattern
description: Implement the strategy pattern using traits and trait objects in Rust.

steps.title: Define Strategy Trait
steps.description: Define a trait `SortStrategy` with method `fn sort(&self, data: &mut [i32])`. Implement `BubbleSort` and `QuickSort` structs that implement the trait.

verification.failureMessage: Sort [5,1,9,3,7] with both strategies and print.

steps.title: Context with Strategy
steps.description: Create a `Sorter` struct that holds a `Box<dyn SortStrategy>` and has a `sort(&self, data: &mut [i32])` method that delegates to the strategy. Test with BubbleSort.
hints: The Sorter doesn't know which strategy it's using.

verification.failureMessage: Use Sorter with BubbleSort and print sorted data.

steps.title: Switch Strategies at Runtime
steps.description: Create a Sorter that can switch strategies at runtime via a `set_strategy` method. Sort data first with BubbleSort, then with QuickSort, demonstrating the different strategies.
hints: Call sort, change strategy, call sort again.
Both should produce the same sorted output.

verification.failureMessage: Sort data with BubbleSort, then switch to QuickSort and sort again.

steps.title: Filter Strategy
steps.description: Define a different strategy: `FilterStrategy` with `fn apply(&self, data: &[i32]) -> Vec<i32>`. Implement `EvenFilter` and `GreaterThanFilter(i32)`. Print the results.

steps.title: Strategy with Closures
steps.description: Instead of trait objects, use closures as strategies. Define a `Transformer` struct that takes a closure `Box<dyn Fn(i32) -> i32>`. Apply `|x| x * 2` and `|x| x + 1` to transform [1, 2, 3].
hints: Apply both closures and print results.

verification.failureMessage: Double and increment [1,2,3] using closure strategies.
